subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Giveaway and Lottery Scams
description: A quick, practical guide to Giveaway and Lottery Scams.

hook.text: Congratulations! You've won an iPhone. Just pay $20 for shipping. The iPhone never arrives.

buildup.text: Fake giveaways collect credit card numbers, addresses, and personal data from eager participants.

discovery.text: Scammers impersonate real brands and celebrities. The fake accounts look nearly identical.

twist.text: Some giveaway scams exist purely to harvest data for future, more targeted attacks.

climax.text: No legitimate company asks winners to pay fees before receiving a prize. That's always fraud.

punchline.text: If winning requires paying, you haven't won anything.

quiz.question: What is a key sign that a giveaway is a scam?
options: Winners are asked to pay fees before receiving a prize
